Expectation1: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation1: You get a frantic call from your friend whose car has broken down on the side of the highway late at night, and they need you to come get them immediately.
Expectation2: Maintain a safe and O39ean work environment.
Situation2: You see a coworker about to walk under a suspended load, and you must shout to warn them instantly.
Story:
My phone buzzed in my pocket just as I was sweeping up the last bit of debris on the site. It was late, and the sky was already darkening. I glanced at the screen—my friend’s name flashed, and when I answered, I could hear the panic in his voice. His car had broken down on the highway, miles from anywhere, and he needed me to come get him right away. I promised I’d figure something out, my mind already racing.

As I hung up, I turned to see one of my coworkers, headphones in, heading straight toward a crane lifting a heavy load overhead. My supervisor always drilled into us: safety first, no exceptions. I was supposed to keep the site safe, to watch out for everyone. But my friend was stranded, scared, and counting on me. My heart pounded as I stood frozen, torn between shouting a warning and dashing off to help my friend. Both needed me, right now, and I could feel the weight of their expectations pressing down, demanding I choose.
